proposals.title: Implement packages/core: branded types, positional RNG, hash, and CanonicalEncoder
proposals.why_now: Every other FASE-1 deliverable depends on core. The spec mandates ADR-009 be written and the CanonicalEncoder implemented before any StateHash can exist. The hash function for ADR-002 is DEFINIR and requires an ADR before implementation. No world, domain, application, replay CLI, or invariant test can be built correctly until core provides nominal bigint types (Money, Quantity, Price, Rate), safe-integer Tick, positional rand(), and the canonical encoder. Two ADRs must be authored as part of this task: the hash function algorithm and ADR-009 CanonicalEncoder spec.

proposals.title: Electron scaffolding: secure BrowserWindow, simulation worker, minimal UI, and installer CI pipeline
proposals.why_now: The spec contains a locked sequencing requirement (§14.6): the installer must exist in FASE-1 in minimal form — not at the end. Deferring Electron bootstrap risks discovering native-module ABI issues, electron-builder platform configuration problems, and worker IPC contract gaps too late to fix architecture. The security configuration (contextIsolation:true, nodeIntegration:false, sandbox:true, preload allowlist) is required for INV-29, a FASE-1 acceptance criterion. This work has no dependency on packages/core and can proceed in parallel with IDEA-001.

proposals.title: Implement packages/world price generator with 2 assets and 2 noise layers
proposals.why_now: FASE-1 requires a price generator covering at least two assets (ORB and NEXA) and two fractal noise layers (trendLayer and idiosyncraticNoise). With core in place this becomes buildable. The octave count, periods, and amplitudes are DEFINIR items requiring an ADR before implementation to avoid embedding unregistered numbers with determinism effect. INV-02 (direct price query equals tick-by-tick arrival) is the most critical invariant in the project per the spec and must be verified before FASE-1 can be accepted.

proposals.title: Implement tick loop, save/load (ADR-006), and tools/replay divergence CLI
proposals.why_now: FASE-1 requires the canonical 10-step tick processing order (§7, TRAVADO) implemented at a single readable point, a save file conforming to ADR-006 (masterSeed + action log + finalTick), and tools/replay reporting the first divergent tick between two executions. Without these, INV-01 (replay purity) and INV-21 (finalTick integrity) cannot be tested and the CI gate cannot run the three reference-game replay comparisons required by §17. This also unblocks tools/bench calibration ratios, which must be frozen before FASE-1 is accepted.

repository_assessment.current_state: Monorepo scaffold is complete: all 16 package directories exist, strict TypeScript compilation, ESLint determinism-enforcement rules, dependency boundary checker, and CI gates are all in place (TASK-0001 and TASK-0002 accepted). Every package source is a stub `export {}`. No production logic, no ADRs, and no invariant tests exist.
repository_assessment.highest_priority_gap: packages/core has zero implementation. It is the direct dependency of every other FASE-1 deliverable. No branded bigint types, positional RNG, canonical encoder, or arithmetic helpers exist, which blocks world, domain, application, replay CLI, bench, and all invariant tests.

warnings: ADR-009 (CanonicalEncoder) is explicitly required by the spec to be written and the encoder implemented before any StateHash exists (§15 FASE-1 acceptance). Producing any StateHash before that ADR is registered is a specification violation, not a sequencing preference.

The hash function for ADR-002 is marked DEFINIR. rand() cannot be implemented before registering the chosen algorithm bit-by-bit in an ADR. Implementing the RNG without this ADR embeds an unregistered number with determinism effect, violating §19 and §16 item 7.

ADR-004 rounding-mode enforcement mechanism is DEFINIR. Domain arithmetic cannot be written until the technical enforcement approach (lint rule, type-level error, or both) is specified in an ADR; without it the invariant exists in name only.

The spec (§5.1) requires transcendental functions in the price generator to be implemented in fixed-point or by linearly interpolated lookup table with identical results on any platform. Math.sin/exp/log/pow are prohibited in pure packages. An ADR must document the chosen approach before world price implementation begins.

tools/bench must establish calibration ratios and freeze them in a versioned file during FASE-1 (§18 baseline protocol). These cannot be frozen until core and world exist, so bench work is sequentially blocked by IDEA-001 and IDEA-002 but must not be deferred past FASE-1 acceptance.
